_: Text of the README 'How it works' figure (v2/where-chock-sits.png), read by render.mjs. Agent names: clients in src/chock/data/witnesses.json. Stops: policies with status production in chock-catalog registry.yaml (rel12-catalog) that stay production after CAT-S1; 'in-agent' marks a best-effort tool-call guard (registry enforcement: advise), 'commit' a gate that blocks.
title: You keep working with your agent as before. Chock checks each action before it lands.

you.name: You
you.line: ask your coding agent for a change

agent.name: Your agent
agent.line: edits files, runs commands and commits

chock.name: Chock checks the action
chock.line: on your machine and in your pipeline, with no model and no tokens

points.name: In CI, on the pull request

outcomes.name: Refused
outcomes.line: the agent is told in one line what to do instead, and tries again

stops.line: a password or API key written into code
a container that runs as root or uses a floating image tag such as latest
a download piped straight into a shell
data sent to a host you have not approved
the agent weakening the checks that review its work (asks you first)

footer: The rules are files in your repository. A person turns them on once with chock sync.
alt: A left-to-right diagram: you ask your coding agent for a change; Chock checks each action before the agent's tool runs where the agent has hooks, at git commit and in CI; an allowed change lands, and a refused one tells the agent in one line what to do instead.
